# What does this PR do?

Support RL gradient-buffer offload when legacy DDP uses NCCL user-buffer registration (UBR).

The affected path is selected by:

```text
--perform-rl-step
--rl-offload-optimizer-during-inference
--use-nccl-ub
```

For this non-CUDA-graph RL path, persistent parameters and disposable gradients receive separate NCCL memory pools. Offload deregisters and releases only the gradient pool; restore recreates gradient storage in a new pool and explicitly registers it with the same data-parallel communicator. Parameter storage stays registered at the same address.

MXFP8 layouts that alias parameter and gradient storage are rejected because those lifetimes cannot be separated.

## Why?

Today, parameters and gradients share one registered pool. Shrinking gradient storage does not release that pool while parameter storage remains live. Restore then grows the storage outside the old pool context, so the replacement address is not explicitly registered.

Training can therefore continue with correct gradients while silently losing both requested properties:

- the old pool retains the released gradient segment instead of returning it for inference;
- restored gradient collectives no longer use explicitly registered storage.

This is a lifecycle and capacity bug, not a crash or numerical-corruption claim.

## Implementation

- Separate non-mutating configuration validation from runtime finalization. `initialize_megatron()` calls `container.finalize()` before runtime services, distributed initialization, and RNG seeding. Finalization applies RNG derivations and, only for RL runs, the required `grad_buffer_offload` layout to the owned `cfg.ddp`; both model-construction paths consume that same configuration without copies. Explicit layout requests are preserved, and CUDA-graph RL does not require gradient-buffer offload.
- Finalization applies runtime derivations once. Subsequent calls are no-ops to support initialization re-entry; use a fresh container for a differently configured run. This repeated-call policy is explicitly raised in the review discussion.
- Split pools only for the registered offload-capable layout; ordinary allocation and other UBR users keep their existing layout.
- Validate every registered buffer and complete all gradient-pool deregistrations before mutating storage. If deregistration fails partway through, storage remains intact but earlier deregistrations are not undone; the run must abort rather than retry offload or reuse the model.
- Drop the old gradient-pool owner after its storage is released; no process-wide `gc.collect()` is needed.
- Allocate and explicitly register the initial replaceable gradient pool, so construction fails rather than retaining an unregistered pool. Restore likewise allocates replacement storage inside a new pool and registers it explicitly. This is deliberate: the existing `nccl_mem` context suppresses registration `RuntimeError`, which is unsafe at either lifecycle boundary. A restore registration failure leaves the buffer offloaded and retryable.
- Add registration/restore error context with exception notes, preserving the original exception type, including CUDA out-of-memory errors.
- Deregister every distinct live pool during shutdown.
- Preserve the existing default gradient-content contract: offload discards and restore zeros gradient contents.

Draft #7383 separately proposes opt-in gradient-content preservation by changing the same private offload/reload helpers. The contracts are independent, but whichever PR lands second will need a semantic rebase; this PR does not claim automatic compatibility with that draft.

## Behavior and cost

This makes the three requested options honor registered-buffer ownership; it is not a blanket speedup. The measurements below are historical evidence from earlier revisions of the same lifecycle design, not performance measurements of the current head.

A paired same-node 128 MiB reduce-scatter probe measured the unfixed post-restore path 10.17% slower than its own pre-offload path. The fixed path changed by 0.007%, and its post-restore service was 7.52% faster than the unfixed post-restore path.

The correct transition has a real cost because it deregisters, destroys, recreates, and registers a pool. In a synthetic stock-`train_rl.py` GRPO comparison, fixed local and symmetric registration were respectively 0.9% and 2.7% slower end to end than the unfixed path. The tradeoff is restored registration and usable inference headroom: a capacity probe exposed 2.1035 GiB more memory per rank and completed a common 73.5 GiB inference allocation that the unfixed path could not allocate.

## Validation

Current published head: `132af3eba91cbd7c8415058579f3682648f74c2d`. The branch is based on upstream `e30d863a6d82a3c45f2d71355dc73fbf5610967b`; this is a pinned base, not a claim that it is the latest main.

### Latest local validation

The lifecycle implementation published in `108ccf7e479eb3698ad96856170d2a88468d30bc` passed:

- 460 selected tests on each of eight GB200 ranks across two nodes (Blyris job `50640`), covering training configuration, RNG ownership, initialization ordering, profiling/logging ownership, inference initialization, autotune configuration, and RL gradient-buffer offload;
- non-mutating repeated validation, once-only finalization, rejection before runtime derivation, serialization/reload behavior, and use of the owned DDP configuration;
- real post-restore collectives, initial-registration and restore failure paths, partial deregistration failure, cleanup checks, and preservation of the original CUDA OOM exception;
- repository-pinned Black, isort, Ruff, and Pylint (10/10) in the changed core/test Python scope, plus `git diff --check`.

Runtime: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch `2.14.0a0+b2c75dd062.nv26.09`, CUDA 13.4, NCCL 2.31.2, and Transformer Engine `2.19.0+5e52befd`. The run used a PyTorch 26.09-based container with test dependencies added in an isolated environment, not the exact upstream CI image.

Current head `132af3eba` differs from that tested implementation only by a shortened `get_model()` docstring. Whitespace checks passed; GPU tests were not rerun for that docstring-only amendment. Full end-to-end training was not rerun for the configuration lifecycle changes. These results do not claim to fix the earlier upstream CI cleanup timeouts.

### Historical validation

Earlier revisions of the same lifecycle design passed:

- Gaia job `69312`: nine focused cases on each of eight H100 ranks, including registration failure, restore failure/retry, shared-pool rejection, and a real post-restore reduce-scatter;
- a two-node, sixteen-H100 symmetric UBR test: a six-layer BF16 GPT completed train → offload → inference → restore → train with stable parameter pool/address, replacement gradient pools, exact loss, and exact local reduced-gradient shards;
- stock `train_rl.py` with all three triggering flags: four synthetic GRPO iterations on eight H100s with finite loss and zero skipped/NaN updates.

Upstream [CI passed on the earlier head `74ac87c`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/36721973960). That result does not validate the newer commits.

### Current review and CI status

As of October 14, 2026, this PR is open and non-draft at `132af3eba`. The configuration-lifecycle review comments have implementation changes and replies; reviewer confirmation remains outstanding, including the repeated-finalization policy. Earlier passing CI is historical evidence only. Current-head upstream CI success has not been verified; local checks do not replace upstream CI.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: N/A — focused lifecycle/capacity fix.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests (the application and multi-node checks are external reproducible probes, not committed CI recipes)
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation (the internal layout and lifecycle are documented in code)
- [x] I have run the repository formatting and lint checks on the changed files

This fallback does not work. I would say this is a torch bug.

The first thing that `register_mem_pool` does is record the pool's ID in an internal torch bookkeeping dictionary. If `register_mem_pool` fails after that, it does not clear the bookkeeping dictionary.

Instead, what happens is that, as soon as `pool` is garbage-collected (which here happens when we `raise`), we get a C-level crash inside torch.

To resolve this, we would need something like
```
        except RuntimeError:
            # Leave the buffer offloaded so a caller can retry or shut down cleanly.
            self.offload_to_cpu(move_params=False, move_grads=True)
            try:
                nccl_allocator.deregister_mem_pool(pool, self.data_parallel_group)
            except RuntimeError:
                pass
            raise
```

This should probably be reported upstream to torch.

## Strict review summary

**Findings:** CRITICAL: 0 · IMPORTANT: 0 · SUGGESTION: 1

**The one finding:** the new local `param_alloc_context` is dead code. It is set at [param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1220](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1220) and [#L1230](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1230), but nothing ever reads it. The strict rubric requires flagging unused variables. guihong-nv raised the same cleanup in an inline comment on this head. Details and a patch are in the inline comment.

**Overall risk: low.** I found nothing that blocks merge. I did not run any GPU tests. Everything below comes from reading the source.

### What I checked
- **Offload/restore order** ([distributed_data_parallel.py#L773-L810](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/distributed_data_parallel.py#L773-L810)):
  - Offload checks every registered buffer first. It deregisters all gradient pools before touching any storage, then resizes storage to 0, then drops the pool owner.
  - Restore creates a new pool, allocates through `torch.cuda.use_mem_pool`, and registers it explicitly.
  - Parameter pools are never touched.
- **tdene's earlier comments (both fixed in the current code):**
  1. A failed registration is now rolled back with a best-effort deregister before the pool can be released ([#L1735-L1747](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1735-L1747)). A failed restore leaves the buffer offloaded and safe to retry ([#L1785-L1791](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1785-L1791)).
  2. The parameter pool is created and registered inside a `try` block, and a failure there rolls back the gradient pool that was already registered ([#L1280-L1294](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1280-L1294)). The parametrized test checks the deregistration order.
- **The new `RuntimeError` can't be hit from in-tree RL code:**
  - Both RL offload sites only offload gradients when `not args.rl_training_cuda_graphs`: [rl_utils.py#L797-L801](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/rl/rl_utils.py#L797-L801) and [#L3031-L3036](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/rl/rl_utils.py#L3031-L3036). That matches the condition in `_configure_grad_buffer_offload`.
  - On the CUDA-graph path, restore falls through to `reload_from_cpu`, which does nothing when nothing was offloaded.
  - `args.grad_buffer_offload` reaches the DDP config through `get_megatron_ddp_config`, which copies fields by name. No auto-generated CLI flag conflicts with it.
- **Rejecting MXFP8 is justified:** in the shared layout, non-quantized parameters are remapped into `param_data`, which is the same storage as `shared_buffer` ([#L1243-L1249](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1243-L1249), [#L1366-L1369](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1366-L1369)). Releasing gradient storage there would also free live parameter storage.
- **Default layouts are unchanged:** without `grad_buffer_offload`, the parameter and gradient buffers are still allocated under one `nccl_mem` or `nullcontext` context ([#L1295-L1299](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py#L1295-L1299)).
- **training.py:** nothing else uses the removed `nccl_allocator` import. Shutdown now deregisters every distinct live pool ([training.py#L5510-L5513](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/74ac87c6071eaca6e8f35671306bf196885207c1/megatron/training/training.py#L5510-L5513)).
- **Manifest:** the new test path passes the `test_manifest.py` checks (the path exists, it is under `tests/unit_tests/`, and tests outside the kernel suite are exempt from the import check).
